what: everything you need to make your number comparable to the reference ones: the id lists each axis is defined on, and the scores themselves
id_column: config, matching the config column of campaign_B.parquet - one simulation
nothing_is_enforced: these are the recipes the reference numbers were made with, not rules. Train on what you like.

reference_split.what: the frozen Campaign B split the reference numbers are scored on
reference_split.test_is_hidden: the test configs are the hidden test set and are not in the public tables; the train configs are all public

ood_split.what: an out-of-distribution split on P_max, the peak plasma pressure
ood_split.how: train one model on the configs in `train` only (P_max below the threshold); drop the public configs above it yourself. With that model, predict test_trajectory.parquet. It is scored twice: on test_indist (the configs below the threshold) and on test_ood (the configs above it, the same ones as test_trajectory_ood.parquet). The result is the gap between the two scores.

plane_holdout.what: the second out-of-distribution axis: positions the model has never seen, on the moment tables
plane_holdout.why_read_separately: seven held-out planes are interpolated across a 0.2 mm gap, but 3.5 sits in a 0.6 mm gap and 5.0 alone in a 2.0 mm one -- a different problem

scores.what: the reference numbers the objectives quote

emulator_inplasma.what: our internal forward emulator on the 357 configurations of test_trajectory.parquet, scored inside the plasma and in the drift after it
emulator_inplasma.zone_rule: in-plasma is z <= L_inj + 3.2 mm per config; a position with fewer than 30 configs of the zone is dropped from both sums
